# Spikes

Research records — a spike answers a question with findings, not code. A spike
closes when the ticket built on its recommendation lands; it is kept where the
reasoning outlives the recommendation. Indexed here under the same two-way
guard as the build layer's own README (`scripts/docs-rules.mjs`).

| Doc | Lifecycle | Purpose | Maturity |
|-----|-----------|---------|----------|
| `spike-vale.md` | ✅ **Finished** — recommendation recorded, rule-shape fix applied same commit | **T-430's findings** — whether the deterministic style checks should run on Vale rather than our own code. Verdict: **adopt later, behind our own rule shape** — Vale cleanly covers two of the four deterministic rule kinds, everything expensive around any engine (config generation, offset mapping, wall-safe workspaces, the coverage statement) is ours to build regardless, its script rule type has no off switch so safety must be by construction, and its one sharp finding was the rule shape: a mixed exceptions field would have made later adoption a migration, so exceptions were split into contexts and terms before any rule exists. Gate for adoption: a pilot firm imports a Vale-format package, or rule sets outgrow the in-house matcher. | 🟢 Findings complete 2026-09-01; **closed same day by the review that landed it** |
| `spike-locators.md` | ✅ **Finished** — built by T-271 | **T-270's findings** — what locator is reliably extractable per format, where the verbatim-passage fallback applies, and the cross-chunk-quote case. Three findings against the running code: a chunk is not a substring of its version, heading numbers are read as sentence terminators, and a cross-boundary quote is in no chunk *and* no version. Kept as the record of **why offsets are stored rather than recovered** — the reasoning outlives the recommendation. Two of its five items are elsewhere by design: the heading split is T-307, PDF input is T-305. | 🟢 Findings complete 2026-08-01; **closed 2026-08-04 by T-271** |
| `spike-authority-corpus.md` | ♻ **Living reference** — recommendation not yet built (T-277 is beyond V1) | **T-276's findings** — the v1 standard-tier instrument list with a licence basis for each, the in-force interval model, and org-tier ingest. Four findings: the standard tier rests on **one** licence basis (Crown copyright / OGL) with three carve-outs that matter more than the list; **"in force" is two time axes**, and the useful one — which cohort of applications an instrument governs — cannot be computed and must be carried as text; the org tier's real problem is **what counts as authority**, enforced by requiring an issuing body, a version and an in-force date at ingest; and the corpus **must not live in `version_chunks`**, whose wall predicate is built for project material. | 🟢 Findings complete 2026-08-27; stays open until T-277 lands |
